prompt:
You are an experienced sommelier comparing two wine recommenders. A
customer with no wine knowledge made this request:

"Can you recommend a sweet red wine from Germany? I want to try something new while watching a film tonight."

List A:
Wine 1: Gewürztraminer, US, $16. Tasting note: "Gewürztraminer has lost some popularity lately, but this is really a lovely wine. It's spiciness and slight sweetness, not to mention the acidity, suggest pairing with today's Asian-inspired fare, especially based around chicken, lamb and pork."
Wine 2: Muscat Hamburg, Ukraine, $9. Tasting note: "This ruby-red sweet wine is nonvintage made and from Muscat Hamburg. It has aromas of cassis syrup and freshly ground dried herbs. In the mouth, there are flavors of sweet ripe cherry preserves, blackberry sauce and sweet pomegranate juice."
Wine 3: Cabernet Sauvignon, US, $13. Tasting note: "As you might infer from the name, this tastes sweet. It appeals to consumers who enjoy the trend of sugary red wines. You could almost drink it as a dessert sipper, with its candied blackberry and cherry flavors."
Wine 4: Red Blend, Turkey, $25. Tasting note: "Deep cherry-red in the glass, this wine proffers a bouquet of strawberry, coffee bean and anise. It is very bright for a red wine and a touch tart, with flavors of cranberry, eucalyptus and mocha. Almost imperceptible tannins linger through the zesty finish."
Wine 5: Red Blend, Italy, $11. Tasting note: "Here's a great deal from central Italy. Dark with mature fruit and spice, this easy red wine would pair with pork or white meat. It offers a pleasing touch of rich sweetness on the close."

List B:
Wine 1: Rhône-style Red Blend, US, $20. Tasting note: "Here's a good, rather standard Rhône-style blend that can serve as an everyday house red wine. It's rich in raspberry and cherry fruit, cherry liqueur and sandalwood flavors, and is easy to like."
Wine 2: Cabernet Sauvignon, US, $32. Tasting note: "Pretty good red wine here, nice and juicy, with well-etched flavors of blackberries and tobacco. The texture is especially pleasing and limpid. Needs an extra edge of depth and complexity to hit the big time, but it sure is delicious."
Wine 3: Red Blend, US, $36. Tasting note: "With flavors of black pepper, sweet charred meat, blackberry jam and toasty oak, this is a seriously good wine, reminiscent of the Northern Rhône. There's a streak of tart red cherries and cola that make this luscious wine enjoyable now."
Wine 4: Riesling, Germany, $92. Tasting note: "Vivid with acidity yet deep and rich in body, this dry, voluptuous wine brings out the best of a difficult vintage for Germany. It's fresh on the palate with bright apple and pear flavors, touched with nuances of bramble, spice, pollen and caramel that add complexity to the long finish."
Wine 5: G-S-M, US, $36. Tasting note: "What a great red wine for drinking now. It has the structure of a fine Merlot, soft and refined, yet the flavors are pure Southern Rhône. There's an umami smoked meatiness to the blackberry jam and black currant fruit, while a touch of oak adds just the right note of sweet toast."

Which list answers the request better as a whole: relevance to every wish,
variety where the request leaves room, and fit for any occasion? If they
are equally good, say tie. Think briefly, then answer with JSON only:
{"reason": "<two sentences at most>", "better": "A" | "B" | "tie"}
